quizzes.stem: A support agent's loop ends when the reply text contains "Case closed", a phrase the prompt tells the model to write last. In testing, some refunds are never issued, because the model writes the phrase in the same reply as the refund call. Which redesign fits best?

options.a: Let the stop value of each response decide, and run every tool request it holds
options.b: Tell the model in the prompt to write its closing phrase only in a final message
options.c: Search the text for more completion phrases, such as "finished" and "complete"
options.d: Call the model a fixed number of times, large enough for the longest case

explanation.a: The model ends its turn by not asking for a tool, and the stop reason reports exactly that, so a reply that holds a tool call is not the end whatever its text says.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a closing phrase in the prompt keeps the control flow in the text: a control flow that needs a particular word "moves the loop's logic into the prompt, where nobody tests it."
explanation.c: Ruled out because more phrases do not make the text a protocol: "It changes with the model, the prompt, the language and the day."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a fixed count is the second anti-pattern: "A task that needs six steps is cut off in the middle".

quizzes.stem: An insurance agent stops after ten model calls and files every run that reaches that cap as cut off. Auditors find complete answers filed this way whenever a case needed exactly ten calls. Which change fits best?

options.a: Raise the cap by one for these particular cases
options.b: Drop the cap and let every run continue
options.c: Compare the tally with the limit before each new request
options.d: Report `done` for any run whose last reply holds some text

explanation.c: The page says the count "is checked before the next call, so that a reply that ends the turn on the very last allowed call is still `done`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says to leave the number alone: "When the status `max_turns` shows up often, the count is not the thing to change."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a run that never converges needs something to stop it: "A count is added so that a run that does not converge is stopped."
explanation.d: Ruled out because text alone does not show an ending: "the text in front of a `tool_use` block is narration, and only the reply that ends the turn holds the answer."

quizzes.stem: A custom tool `deduct_stock` writes to inventory, and a custom tool `notify_warehouse` reads the new level. The model asks for both in one turn, and the developer marks only `notify_warehouse` as read-only to save time. What can the team count as guaranteed?

options.a: That the write finishes first, since state-changing tools always run ahead of any readers
options.b: Nothing, since simultaneous requests have no promised order and need separate rounds
options.c: That both run in the order requested, since every custom tool runs one after another here
options.d: That the reader waits, since the SDK works out the dependency from the tool names

explanation.b: The page says to put a dependency in two turns, because the model decides what to ask for in one turn and the SDK promises no order between the calls it makes together.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the documented rule is about conflicts among tools that change state: "Tools that modify state (like Edit, Write, and Bash) run sequentially to avoid conflicts."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a tool marked read-only is allowed to run alongside others: "To enable parallel execution for a custom tool, set readOnlyHint in its annotations."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the SDK does not read names for dependencies: "a dependency belongs in two turns."

quizzes.stem: A finance dashboard reads the `usage` field of every result to report what agent runs cost, but the invoices are higher for the runs that delegated to subagents. What explains the gap, and what is the fix?

options.a: Add the cost of the helpers by parsing their own messages out of the stream
options.b: Treat the figure as complete and look for unlogged retries in the application
options.c: It covers only the lead loop, so consult the per-model accounting for the whole tree
options.d: The figure is zeroed whenever a run is cut off, so leave those runs out

explanation.c: The `usage` figure counts one loop only, and the page names the field for the whole tree.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the SDK already provides that accounting: "Use `modelUsage`, or `model_usage` in Python, for whole-tree token and cost accounting."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the figure is incomplete by design: "A run that delegated to subagents has spent more than `usage` says."
explanation.d: Ruled out because zeroed figures belong to a crash and not to a cut-off: "the final result is an `error_during_execution` whose cost fields may be zeroed".

quizzes.stem: A team's runs often end with the status `max_turns` because one tool keeps failing, and raising the cap from ten to forty only made each failed run cost four times as much. What should they do?

options.a: Turn the cap off entirely and let the model decide when a failure is final
options.b: Raise the cap again and again until the failures stop ending in the cap itself
options.c: Read the saved conversation, then repair that helper's description

explanation.c: The status is a signal about a run that does not converge, and the conversation shows why.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the count is not what is wrong: "The status is a signal to read the conversation, which the practice keeps whole for that reason."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a run needs a backstop: "A count is added so that a run that does not converge is stopped."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the count "has its own status", and reporting `done` for it hides the problem that the fixed loop also hides.

quizzes.stem: A loop that follows this module's practice receives a reply whose stop reason asks for a tool, but its content holds only a sentence of text. What should it do?

options.a: Send an empty user message and call the model once more to see what it does
options.b: Finish with a malformed status and make no further call
options.c: Return the sentence to the user as the finished answer
options.d: Call the model again with the same messages and hope for a call

explanation.b: There is nothing to answer, and the practice stops with its own status.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the API does not accept it: "an empty message, which a loop can send by accident when a `tool_use` reply holds no call, is refused."
explanation.c: Ruled out because narration is not an answer: "Only the reply that ends the turn holds the answer."
explanation.d: Ruled out because guessing is what the loop avoids: "A value the loop has never seen must not be guessed at."

quizzes.stem: A dashboard alerts on every run that ends with a null stop reason and zero cost, and the team suspects a parsing bug. What explains those runs?

options.a: A turn limit, which can report a zero cost for the unfinished run of the agent
options.b: A refusal by the model, which is reported with a null stop reason at first sight
options.c: A normal run that has no stop reason to give
options.d: A crashed session, which closes in an error result whose figures may be blanked

explanation.d: The documentation describes this result for a crash: "the final result is an `error_during_execution` whose cost fields may be zeroed and whose `stop_reason` is `null`".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a refusal sets the reason: "Claude declined to respond."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a normal end carries a value: "Claude finished its response naturally."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a run that the loop ends has a value: "`stop_reason` carries the value from the last assistant response before the loop ended".
